surprises.description: Xylem cut FY2026 revenue guidance to about $8.95 billion, roughly flat organically, from prior guidance of 2%–3% organic growth. That also reverses the preview’s implied Q4 ramp: Q4 revenue is now expected to decline 1%–2% organically rather than support roughly 5% reported growth.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Lowered its full year 2026 revenue guidance to approximately $8.95 billion (down ~1% reported, roughly flat organically) from prior guidance of 2%-3% organic growth, due to slower revenue conversion in MCS and WSS”; Q4 revenue is “expected down ~5% reported (down 1%-2% organic).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed FY26 organic growth guidance of “+2–3%” and said the FY guide implied “Q4 ≈ $2,439M, or ~+5% reported.”

surprises.description: Full-year EPS guidance fell to $5.40–$5.45 from $5.55–$5.70, a clear reversal of the prior raised outlook. The preview treated the prior range as the current guide and anticipated that a narrowed range might land in its upper half.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full year EPS guidance was cut to $5.40-$5.45 from the prior $5.55-$5.70, reflecting lower volumes while holding margins.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview gave FY26 adjusted EPS guidance as “$5.55 – $5.70” and described a base case in which “FY EPS range [is] narrowed to the upper half.”

surprises.description: Q3 revenue was roughly flat organically and below expectations, missing the preview’s expectation of about 3% organic growth. The gap is notable because the preview identified organic growth as the central test for the quarter.
surprises.fact_evidence: Q3 revenue came in “roughly flat organically and below expectations.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview expected Q3 guidance of “~+3% organic” and called for “organic growth ≥3% vs. guide.”

surprises.description: Demand indicators were stronger than the preview’s expectation for mid-single-digit underlying order growth: total orders rose 10%, backlog grew 13% to $5.5 billion, and book-to-bill was above 1. The contrast is that this demand is not yet converting into revenue at the expected pace.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Total orders rose 10% year-over-year and backlog grew 13% to $5.5 billion (up ~$200 million sequentially), with book-to-bill above 1.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said the Q3 question was whether “core orders inflect to mid-single-digits without a mega-deal” and highlighted book-to-bill above 1.0x as a bull trigger.

surprises.description: MCS orders surged 30%, but revenue fell 5% as affordability concerns spread from electric to water metering, and some large awards will not deploy until late 2027 into 2028. The preview noted electric-metering affordability pressure but described water-side orders as an offset, so the extension of the affordability issue to water metering and the delayed conversion worsen that picture.
surprises.fact_evidence: “MCS orders surged 30% with a book-to-bill of 1.16, but revenue fell 5% as affordability pressures that hit electric metering now extend to water metering, with large awards deploying in late 2027 into 2028.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said MCS faced “electric-metering affordability concerns” and that “Water-side orders grew double digits, partly offsetting.”

surprises.description: Xylem announced plans to divest two additional businesses—Applied Water International and Specialty Flow Control—together about 9% of revenue but less than 5% of EBITDA. The preview discussed the already-completed international metrology divestiture, but did not anticipate these new planned disposals or the resulting reduction in China exposure.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Plans to divest Applied Water International and Specialty Flow Control (beverage and marine), which together represent ~9% of revenue but less than 5% of EBITDA and are dilutive to margins, cutting China exposure from ~2% to ~1% of revenue.”

surprises.description: Xylem will consolidate from four segments to three beginning in 2027 and eliminate Water Infrastructure segment support costs. The preview discussed segment performance and a possible MCS margin step-up, but did not flag this broader organizational change.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company will consolidate from 4 segments to 3 beginning in 2027, aligning around how customers move, treat, and measure/optimize water, and eliminating Water Infrastructure segment support costs.”

surprises.description: Q3 adjusted EPS of $1.44 was slightly below the $1.45 consensus and further below the preview’s $1.47 top-of-guide “de facto whisper,” despite 5% year-over-year growth.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 EPS grew 5% year-over-year to $1.44 (excluding IEEPA tariff refund).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed Q3 consensus adjusted EPS of “$1.45” and said “the de facto whisper is the top of guidance ($1.47).”

surprises.description: Q3 EBITDA margin was 23.9%, modestly above the preview’s 23.7% consensus estimate and at the top end of the company’s prior range, even with revenue below expectations. This partly offsets the weaker sales and EPS results.
surprises.fact_evidence: Q3 EBITDA margin was “23.9%, up 70 basis points.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview estimated Q3 adjusted EBITDA margin at “~23.7%” and cited company guidance of “23.5% – 24.0%.”

surprises.description: Q4 is expected to combine declining organic revenue with a 24.5% EBITDA margin, up 130 basis points year over year. The margin outlook is resilient despite the sharp revenue slowdown, though the preview did not provide a specific Q4 margin estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: Q4 EBITDA margin is expected to be “~24.5% (up 130 bps)” while revenue is expected down 1%–2% organically.

surprises.description: The preview asked whether buybacks would be paused to fund the Cornell/Roper deal or continued; the call described opportunistic buybacks, alongside acquisition-related financing costs, as a factor weighing on free cash flow. This indicates buybacks were still being used even as cash-flow guidance moved to its low end.
surprises.fact_evidence: Year-to-date free cash flow was “$444 million (slightly below last year)” and full-year free cash flow margin guidance was trimmed to “~10.2% at the low end,” reflecting “higher interest from the Cornell and Roper acquisition financing and opportunistic buybacks.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview asked whether the buyback was “paused to fund the deal — or leaned into.”
